### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, five activities — A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 — each took part in roughly 17–25 of 100 traces (33–49 of the 200 traces each). In the later window, none of the five appears in any of the 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Earlier, these five behaved as mutually exclusive alternatives: no trace contained two of them, and their participation shares sum to 100 of 100 traces, so every trace included exactly one of them. In the later window, every trace contains neither activity of any of these pairs. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL001, REL010, REL015, REL019]
- The routing out of A38 changed: earlier, A38's observed outgoing transitions split across the five activities (A21 about 25 in 100, A14 about 22, A22 about 20, A15 about 18, A20 about 17), and each of the five led only onward to A23. In the later window, A38 leads directly to A23 in all observed cases. [DIR006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- The distance from A38 to A23 changed from always two positions (one activity in between) to always one position (directly consecutive). [LAG001]
- A23 and A39 still occur in every trace in both windows; A23's relative position moved slightly earlier (mean about 0.40 to about 0.38 of the trace length). [POS006, REL007, REL022]
- A41 and A42 now each appear in about 67 of 100 traces, up from about 53 of 100 earlier; their co-occurrence with the five vanished activities (about 9–13 of 100 traces before) fell to zero. [REL008, REL009, REL013, REL014, REL017, REL018, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the five-way choice segment between A38 and A23 — the mutually exclusive activities A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 — is bypassed in the later window: earlier, every trace moved from A38 through exactly one of the five and then to A23, two positions apart, while in the later window A38 is followed immediately by A23 in every trace and none of the five is observed. The screening produced 44 qualifying items against roughly 0.54 expected for an unchanged process, so the ensemble is not what a stable process typically yields; the rerouting is shown directly at A38 and in the A38–A23 distance, the five activities fall from 33–49 supporting traces to zero, and the relation and position items consistently describe the same rerouting. This is a possibility supported by the evidence, not a confirmed modification. [DIR006, LAG001, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL005, REL006, REL020, REL021, POS006]

Limitations: zero participation establishes only that the five activities were not observed later, so the evidence cannot distinguish permanent removal from a routing change that skips the block in all observed cases, nor show whether the block's work moved elsewhere. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the case mix between the windows (for example, a later sample drawn only from case types that never used this segment); the earlier participation of about 17–25 in 100 traces per activity makes pure chance absence in 200 later traces implausible, but a systematic subpopulation shift cannot be excluded. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR006, LAG001]

Other differences: A41 and A42 each rose from about 53 to about 67 of 100 traces, an increase the bypass hypothesis does not explain; A23's relative position also shifted slightly earlier, consistent with the shorter traces. [REL008, REL009, REL013, REL014, REL017, REL018, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, POS006]
